title: New Residential Sales (November 2026 data) — 10:00 a.m. ET, the 17th-workday twin of housing starts and the last Census print of 2026
source: CENSUS: two independent census.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research — economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes, 179 rows parsed), row "New Residential Sales | December 23, 2026 | 10:00 AM | November 2026", release code A202612231000, reference A202611; and construction/soc/schedule.html (HTTP 200, 59,625 bytes), the Survey of Construction's own program schedule, whose terminal row reads "November 2026 | December 17, 2026 | December 23, 2026" under the column head "(17th Workday) Revised Building Permits - 8:00 a.m. / New Residential Sales - 10:00 a.m.". Corroborated twice more: census.gov/construction/xls/historic_release_dates.xls (HTTP 200, 55,808 bytes, 515 rows 1984-01 → 2026-11), whose terminal row reads reference 2026-11 → NRC 2026-12-17, NRS 2026-12-23; and the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet (HTTP 200, 16,944 bytes), whose 2026-12-23 10:00 row names "New-home sales". Promoted estimate → confirmed on the two-primary precedent this calendar carries for durable-goods-2026-12-23 and housing-starts-2026-12-17. TWO BOUNDARIES ON THE WORD, inherited verbatim from the 12-23 siblings: `confirmed` describes the published schedule as of 2026-09-06, not immunity from a re-dating, and emphatically not immunity from the funding branch in the notes — a lapse-driven slip is a schedule change Census makes unilaterally and this label does not price it. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: THE MORE EXPOSED HALF OF THE 12-17/12-23 PAIR, AND THE ONE PRECEDENT SAYS GETS CAUGHT. Initial research 2026-09-06 (docs/research/events/new-home-sales-2026-12-23.md) wrote this canonical file after reading the single proposal (from-housing-starts-2026-12-17), now shadowed. Three findings the proposal did not carry. (1) THE SCHEDULE STATISTIC DOES NOT TRANSFER FROM THE SIBLING. New Residential Sales ran a DIFFERENT schedule before 2001 — 78 of 202 pre-2001 editions published two months after their reference month — so the housing-starts lane's "9 of 514 slips since 1984" is not this series' number. On the modern 17th-workday regime (reference 2000-12 onward, n=312) NRS slipped out of the month after its reference month 12 times against its New Residential Construction twin's 9, and the THREE EXTRA SLIPS ARE EXACTLY CASES WHERE THE TWIN PRINTED ON TIME AND THIS ONE DID NOT (reference 2013-10, 2018-11, 2026-03). All 12 belong to the three federal funding lapses; nothing else has ever moved this schedule. (2) THE 2018 PRECEDENT IS THIS PRINT'S EXACT GEOMETRY. The Nov-2018 edition was due on the 17th workday, 2018-12-26; the lapse began 2018-12-22; it published 2019-01-31, a 36-day slip — while its NRC twin had printed on time on 2018-12-18, four days before onset. In 2026 the same pair straddles cr-expiry-2026-12-11 the same way: NRC 12-17 is 6 days past it, this print is 12. (3) THE NOWCAST LINE — the one thing the corridor says is worth reading off this release — IS UNREADABLE ON THIS DATE. The Atlanta Fed's 2026-12-23 10:00 vintage carries "GDP (Q3 3rd estimate), Personal income and outlays, NIPA underlying detail tables, Advance Census manufacturing (M3-1), New-home sales"; across the 10 historical vintages of that exact configuration the residential contribution was the LARGEST of the eight component moves 0 times (PCE 7, inventories 2, net exports 1), and the headline moved 0.4207pp against 0.0528pp on a solo new-home vintage. Impact LOW and symbols empty on measured grounds, not assumption: on Census's own 515 real release dates the overnight gap is null (ITB p=0.84, XHB p=0.72 — correct for a 10:00 print) and the session-range effect that was real through 2015 (ITB 2010-15 2.443% vs 2.063%, p=0.0061) has been null for eleven years (2016-20 p=0.36, 2021-26 p=0.30); no macro- or housing-keyed house playbook exists (re-grepped 2026-09-06, 0 hits). Nothing here licenses an entry and there is no instrument to enter.
